newsitem.title: FRANCE: Communist Gayssot gave name to anti-racism law.
newsitem.headline: Communist Gayssot gave name to anti-racism law.

text.p: Communist Jean-Claude Gayssot, appointed France's minister of infrastructure, transport and housing on Wednesday, is best known for co-authoring a tough anti-racism law which critics say limits freedom of speech.

He will be the senior Communist in Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's Socialist-led government, inheriting ultra-sensitive issues such as the future of state-owned airline Air France which the centre-right government had planned to privatise.

Gayssot, 52, a former railway technician who worked his way up through party and union ranks as a full-time apparatchik in what was long the most Stalinist party in Western Europe, will also be in charge of the loss-making SNCF state railways.
He joined the Communist Party in 1963 and was first active in the powerful CGT trade union controlled by the Communists.
He became a full-time member of the party national executive in 1976 and was elected to its ruling, internal secretariat in 1991.
The law which Gayssot proposed with former Socialist prime minister Laurent Fabius in 1990 sharply increased punishments for making racist statements.
It has been used several times against publications close to anti-immigrant leader Jean-Marie Le Pen's National Front party.
First elected to parliament in 1986, Gayssot has been regularly re-elected since as a member for the working class Saint-Denis suburb of Paris, a traditional Communist bastion.
